newsitem.title: POLAND: Poland's c.bank has no comment on PBI sale report.
newsitem.headline: Poland's c.bank has no comment on PBI sale report.

text.p: The National Bank of Poland would not confirm a newspaper report that it had shortlisted three banks bidding for the Polish Investment Bank (PBI) and Prosper Bank, the NBP's deputy president said on Friday.

Rzeczpospolita daily newspaper said earlier on Friday that the central bank, which controls both the PBI and Prosper Bank, shortlisted Kredyt Bank, GE Capital and Creditanstalt Bank SA as potential investors.
"Some of the informations (in the report) are true, some are false, so as a whole this is not true," Witold Kozinski told Reuters over the phone.
Rzeczpospolita also said that the bank would choose the final bid in January 1997 at the earliest. It gave no sources.
The newspaper also said that the GE Capital bid was considered as most attractive.

PBI, recently awarded a BBB- long-term rating by IBCA, made an 85.1-million-zloty pre-tax profit over the first three quarters of 1996 and expected to make a pre-tax profit of 100 million this year and a net profit of more than 60 million.
Last year PBI had a net profit of 26.2 million zlotys.
PBI, carved out of the NBP in 1993 with a clean credit portfolio, remains 100-percent owned by the central bank
The NBP took control of more than 90 percent of ailing Prosper Bank in 1993 as a result of a bail-out scheme and has since retained its stake to guide the bank's turnaround.
